h: More of the Dukeries to Explore
p: Sherwood Pines sits right in the heart of the area known as the Dukeries, named after the great estates once owned by dukes, and several of them make brilliant days out today. Clumber Park, cared for by the National Trust, has a huge lake, a long avenue of lime trees and plenty of space for walking and cycling. Rufford Abbey Country Park, with its abbey ruins, gardens and lake, is another easy follow-up, and it's handy for families with younger children.

A little further south, Newstead Abbey was once the home of the poet Lord Byron, with beautiful gardens and grounds around the historic house. In Nottingham itself, the castle and the network of man-made caves under the city are well worth a look if you're stopping for longer.

For your treetop session, allow a couple of hours, and plan your arrival around the forest's popularity. Sherwood Pines is very busy in the school holidays, so give yourself time to park and find the meeting point. The course gets you moving, so dress in layers you can take off, and keep a dry top in the car.
First-timers should take the early crossings slowly, get used to the clip-on routine and build confidence as they go. By the final zip wire most people are itching to have another go.
Edwinstowe village is close by, with cafés and pubs for a well-earned refuel before heading home.
